The [taxonomy](/wiki/Taxonomy_(biology) "Taxonomy (biology)") of the genus is complicated. The first issue is whether the name should more properly be *Amaryllis* L.. In 1753 [Carl Linnaeus](/wiki/Carl_Linnaeus "Carl Linnaeus") created the name *[Amaryllis belladonna](/wiki/Amaryllis_belladonna "Amaryllis belladonna")*, the [type species](/wiki/Type_species "Type species") of the genus *[Amaryllis](/wiki/Amaryllis "Amaryllis")*, in his *[Species Plantarum](/wiki/Species_Plantarum "Species Plantarum")* along with eight other *Amaryllis* species.[[b]](#cite_note-43)[[42]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELinnaeus1753[httpswwwbiodiversitylibraryorgpage358106page304mode1up_''Amaryllis''_pp. 292–293]-44) Linnaeus had earlier worked on the Estate of [George Clifford](/wiki/George_Clifford_III "George Clifford III") near [Haarlem](/wiki/Haarlem "Haarlem") between 1735 and 1737 describing the plants growing there in his *[Hortus Cliffortianus](/wiki/Hortus_Cliffortianus "Hortus Cliffortianus")* in 1738.[[43]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJarvis2016-45) It is to this work that he refers in his *Species Plantarum*.[[44]](#cite_note-Linn37-46) This was assumed to be the South African Cape Belladonna, although not precisely known.[[41]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESealy1939-42) Clifford's herbarium is now preserved at the [Natural History Museum](/wiki/Natural_History_Museum,_London "Natural History Museum, London") in London.[[43]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJarvis2016-45)

At the time both South African and South American plants were placed in this same genus. By the early nineteenth century *Amaryllis* had become a [polymorphic](/wiki/Polymorphism_(biology) "Polymorphism (biology)") (diverse) genus with about 50 species from what we would consider a dozen genera today, and attempts were made to separate it into different genera.[[41]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESealy1939-42) This work commenced in 1819 with the contributions of the English botanist, the Revd. The **mayor of the City of San Diego** is the official head and chief executive officer of the U.S. city of [San Diego](/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"), California. The mayor has the duty to enforce and execute the laws enacted by the [San Diego City Council](/wiki/San_Diego_City_Council "San Diego City Council"), the legislative branch. The mayor serves a four-year term and is limited to two successive terms.

There have been 36 people who have served as mayor in San Diego since 1850, when [California](/wiki/California "California") became a state following the [Conquest of California](/wiki/Conquest_of_California "Conquest of California"). Prior to the conquest, [Californios](/wiki/Californios "Californios") served as [mayor of San Diego during the Spanish and Mexican eras](/wiki/List_of_pre-statehood_mayors_of_San_Diego "List of pre-statehood mayors of San Diego") since 1780. From 1852 to 1888, the city was run by a board of trustees and there was no elected mayor. However, the president of the board was called *mayor* as a courtesy.

The most recent election was held in [November 2024](/wiki/2024_San_Diego_mayoral_election "2024 San Diego mayoral election"), and [Todd Gloria](/wiki/Todd_Gloria "Todd Gloria") was re-elected as the 37th mayor of San Diego.

**Kangchenjunga** is the [third-highest mountain in the world](/wiki/List_of_highest_mountains_on_Earth "List of highest mountains on Earth"). Its summit lies at 8,586 m (28,169 ft) in a section of the [Himalayas](/wiki/Himalayas "Himalayas"), the *Kangchenjunga Himal*, which is bounded in the west by the [Tamur River](/wiki/Tamur_River "Tamur River"), in the north by the [Lhonak River](/wiki/Lhonak_River "Lhonak River") and [Jongsang La](/wiki/Jongsong_Peak "Jongsong Peak"), and in the east by the [Teesta River](/wiki/Teesta_River "Teesta River"). It lies in the border region between [Koshi Province](/wiki/Koshi_Province "Koshi Province") of [Nepal](/wiki/Nepal "Nepal") and [Sikkim](/wiki/Sikkim "Sikkim") state of [India](/wiki/India "India"), with the West and Kangbachen peaks located in Nepal's [Taplejung District](/wiki/Taplejung_District "Taplejung District") and the Main, Central and South peaks directly on the border.

Until 1852, Kangchenjunga was assumed to be the [highest mountain in the world](/wiki/List_of_past_presumed_highest_mountains "List of past presumed highest mountains"). However, precise calculations and meticulous measurements by the [Great Trigonometrical Survey](/wiki/Great_Trigonometrical_Survey "Great Trigonometrical Survey") of India in 1849 showed that [Mount Everest](/wiki/Mount_Everest "Mount Everest"), known as Peak XV at the time, is higher. After allowing for further verification of all calculations, it was officially announced in 1856 that Kangchenjunga is the third-highest mountain in the world.

Kangchenjunga is considered a sacred mountain in Nepal and Sikkim. It was first climbed on 25 May 1955 by [Joe Brown](/wiki/Joe_Brown_(climber) "Joe Brown (climber)") and [George Band](/wiki/George_Band "George Band"), who were part of the [1955 British Kangchenjunga expedition](/wiki/1955_British_Kangchenjunga_expedition "1955 British Kangchenjunga expedition"). Government spending in Singapore has risen since the start of the [2008 financial crisis](/wiki/2008_financial_crisis "2008 financial crisis"), from around 15% of GDP in 2008 to 17% in 2012. It has the third-largest remaining [rainforest](/wiki/Rainforest "Rainforest") globally, and the highest plant biodiversity of any island.[[1]](#cite_note-2) Located in [Melanesia](/wiki/Melanesia "Melanesia") in the southwestern [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean"), the island is separated from [Australia](/wiki/Mainland_Australia "Mainland Australia") by the 150-kilometre (81-nautical-mile; 93-mile) wide [Torres Strait](/wiki/Torres_Strait "Torres Strait"), though both landmasses lie on the same [continental shelf](/wiki/Continental_shelf "Continental shelf"), and were united during episodes of low sea level in the [Pleistocene glaciations](/wiki/Pleistocene_glaciation "Pleistocene glaciation") as the combined landmass of [Sahul](/wiki/Sahul "Sahul"). Numerous smaller islands are located to the west and east.
